title: Toward new energy-rich molecular systems: from N10 to N60

species.method: SCF, B3LYP, MP2, QCISD, cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ bases (Table 1)
species.source_note: Table 1 + Table 2 (frequencies), p. 264 -- confirmed genuine minimum (D2d), companion D2h planar structure is a confirmed saddle point (imaginary freq 75-93 cm-1 depending on method), NOT a minimum

bond_params.note: Two symmetry-inequivalent values given per bond/angle label (two rows per Ri/ai in Table 1) -- likely the two chemically-distinct ring environments of the D2d bicyclic bispentazole structure (bridging bond R2 vs in-ring bonds R1/R3/R4).
bond_params.R2_is_bridging_bond: R2 is explicitly the inter-ring bridging bond (the 'remarkably strong' N-N bond mentioned in the abstract, DE(N10->2N5)=93 kcal/mol at QCISD)

species.notes: Bicyclic N10 = two 5-membered rings joined by a single bridging N-N bond in an orthogonal (D2d) arrangement -- this is almost certainly the SAME topology as N10_D2d_linked5rings / N10_D2d_bispentazole_GS already in the existing biblio_polyN corpus. Treat as a cross-validation / higher-quality alternate literature source for the same structure, not a new topology -- but this paper's multi-method bond-length table (SCF/B3LYP/MP2/QCISD) is notably more rigorous than a single-method source, worth keeping as a reference. A planar D2h isomer is explicitly confirmed as a SADDLE POINT (not a minimum) -- exclude that one from any minima list.

bond_params.shape: 5-membered ring radical, R1/R4 bonds similar to those in the N10 bicyclic structure above, R3 bond much more single-bond-like (elongated) than in N10 -- MP2 tends to open the ring entirely (R3 highly stretched/non-bonded) at that level
bond_params.R1_R4_note: text states R1 and R4 are 'similar' to their N10 counterparts but does not retabulate exact numeric values for this radical -- only R3 is explicitly given

species.notes: Neutral N5 RADICAL (mult=2, doublet) formed by homolytic N10 ring-opening -- distinct from the well-known closed-shell N5+ cation and N5- anion already in the corpus. MP2 level does NOT confirm this as a bonded ring (opens to a non-bonded/highly stretched R3) -- only QCISD/CISD/B3LYP support a closed 5-ring minimum; flag this method-dependence explicitly if pursued further.

species.point_group: not explicitly named in text (analogized to icosahedral C60/buckminsterfullerene -- likely Ih, but VERIFY, not literally stated as 'Ih' in this paper unlike some other archive papers that do call an N60 species D3d etc.)
species.source_note: Table 3, p. 266 -- confirmed as 'a local minimum at the AM1 and SCF levels of theory' per abstract

bond_params.shape: buckminsterfullerene-analog cage (60 atoms), two symmetry-distinct bond types: R1 = pentagonal-ring bonds, R2 = bonds shared between six-membered rings

species.notes: generic_guess shape='cage', n_atoms=60. Proposed by the author to be buildable from 6 units of the D2d bicyclic N10 above (Fig. 2, not read as image). Likely overlaps/duplicates the N60 species already catalogued from other archive papers (N60_marek_03.pdf, N10-N60.pdf is itself one of 2 internal-duplicate-flagged files per the coordinator's dedup list already) and possibly the N60.pdf / N60-livermore.pdf entries -- cross-check point group and bond lengths against those before treating as independently new. No exact point-group symbol given here (only 'icosahedral' analogy in prose) -- do not assume Ih without confirming against a paper that states it explicitly (e.g. the separate N_nanotubes_06.pdf entry in this same archive batch DOES give N60 explicitly as D3d, which conflicts with an Ih assumption -- these may be genuinely different N60 isomers, not the same structure; keep them as SEPARATE candidate species, formula N60 charge 0, until graph-topology comparison proves otherwise.)
